metrics.name: New builds avoided (modelled)
metrics.method: requests whose recommendation is not new_build
metrics.basis: Assumes every recommendation is approved and carried out as recommended.
metrics.caveat: A modelled outcome over the synthetic request log, not a measured saving. Human review counts as avoided here, and a person may still build.

metrics.name: New builds avoided, canonical definitions only
metrics.method: same count, but a primary KPI row on a conflicting or local definition no longer qualifies a target
metrics.basis: Sensitivity check on one rule choice; the rule in use has not changed.
metrics.caveat: Shows how much the headline depends on accepting non-canonical definitions as repairable. Other rule choices were not varied.

metrics.name: Requests in the data pack
metrics.method: 150 business requests from 10 distinct texts
metrics.basis: The data pack's Business_Requests sheet as given.
metrics.caveat: Repeated texts with different products and markets, so 150 decisions are not 150 independent cases.

metrics.name: Citations checked
metrics.method: every cited (table, id) exists in the data pack
metrics.basis: 1098 citations over 150 requests, 0 invalid. Assumes the data pack is the source of truth.
metrics.caveat: A valid citation is a real row, not proof that the row supports the claim.

metrics.name: Specs passing every gate today
metrics.method: new_build and extend specs that pass all 7 gates, with the owner the system proposes
metrics.basis: Today's data pack, owners as recorded.
metrics.caveat: Gates check governance rules, not whether the spec is what the requester wanted.

metrics.name: Specs passing after the SM-065 owner fix (simulated)
metrics.method: 80 SM-065 specs from 7 distinct request texts rerun with an active owner (OWN-039) on SM-065 in memory
metrics.basis: Assumes one active owner is assigned to SM-065; simulated, never written to the data pack. Any of the 47 active owners gives the same result.
metrics.caveat: Modelled specs, not reports anyone has built, and the 80 come from only 7 distinct texts.

metrics.name: Assets in the estate today
metrics.method: Analytics_Assets rows
metrics.caveat: Counts assets, not their quality or use.

metrics.name: Assets after 150 requests, with Reuse Gate (projection)
metrics.method: today + 93 new builds - 2 retired
metrics.basis: Assumes every recommendation is carried out, and human review adds nothing.
metrics.caveat: A projection. The 93 builds cover 67 distinct combinations, so a real team could build fewer.

metrics.name: Assets after 150 requests, with no check (projection)
metrics.method: today + 150 new builds
metrics.basis: Assumes every request becomes one new asset; the data pack does not record what would have happened.
metrics.caveat: An upper-bound projection, not an observed outcome.

metrics.name: Faithfulness (deterministic claim check)
metrics.method: every asset id, KPI name, number and status in the explanation must appear in the decision or the rows it cites
metrics.caveat: Shows that no invented ids, numbers, KPIs or statuses got through. Does not show that the reasoning is right, that a true fact is attached to the right asset, or that the explanation is complete. No AITTA_API_KEY in the environment, so only the saved chip explanations were checked.

metrics.name: Faithfulness (LLM judge)
metrics.method: meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as judge; prompt in data/judge_prompt.txt
metrics.caveat: Not run: no AITTA_API_KEY in the environment. Run scripts/eval_quality.py with the key in the environment.

metrics.name: Guard replacement rate
metrics.method: share of AI explanations the pipeline guard would replace with the rules explanation
metrics.caveat: A low rate shows the generator rarely states unsupported facts on these requests. It depends on the prompt and model of this run, and says nothing about requests unlike these.

metrics.name: Answer relevance
metrics.method: mean share of required items named: the action, the target and each requested KPI
metrics.caveat: Keyword presence, not understanding: an explanation can name everything and still be unclear, and a correct synonym counts as missing.

metrics.name: Context precision
metrics.method: cited rows that belong to the target asset, its semantic model or the model built on, the requested KPIs, or an invoked rule
metrics.basis: 150 batch requests, rules parser. Not counted as relevant: Migration_Backlog 29, Analytics_Assets 20, Asset_Usage 20
metrics.caveat: By this definition, rows about assets listed to retire or consolidate later, and about legacy workbooks in a migration, count as not relevant even though the decision needs them. It shows focus, not whether each row was necessary.

metrics.name: Context recall
metrics.method: required rows present: the target and its usage, its primary KPI map rows, the backlog row for a migration, the model and canonical KPIs for a new build, and at least one rule
metrics.caveat: The required set is our own definition of a minimal justification, written by the same person as the rules, so 100% shows the rules cite what they were designed to cite, not that nothing else was needed.

metrics.name: Intent accuracy, first reading
metrics.method: products, market, KPIs and kind all equal the expected clean intent, before any question
metrics.caveat: The expected intents and the vocabulary were written by the same person, with these prompts in view. Not a measure of unseen language.

metrics.name: Intent accuracy, after the clarification loop
metrics.method: same check after the loop, with answers simulated from the expected intent
metrics.caveat: Answers are simulated and always helpful, so this is a best case for real requesters.

metrics.name: KPI matching precision, first reading
metrics.method: requested KPIs read correctly over all KPIs read, micro-averaged
metrics.caveat: Misspelled and non-English readings are held as proposals and are not counted here until confirmed.

metrics.name: KPI matching recall, first reading
metrics.method: expected KPIs that were read, micro-averaged
metrics.caveat: Same caveat as precision.

metrics.name: KPI matching precision, after the loop
metrics.method: as above, after the loop
metrics.caveat: Simulated answers name the KPIs directly, which makes this easier than real use.

metrics.name: KPI matching recall, after the loop
metrics.method: as above, after the loop
metrics.caveat: Same caveat.

metrics.name: Decision agreement: rules and gpt-oss-120b
metrics.method: same action from the model's intent as from the rule parser's, per distinct request
metrics.caveat: Agreement is not accuracy: there is no ground truth and the model can be right where the rules are not. Measured on the 10 clean texts with an earlier prompt version and pipeline.

metrics.name: Decision agreement: rules and GLM-5.2
metrics.method: same action from the model's intent as from the rule parser's, per distinct request
metrics.caveat: Agreement is not accuracy: there is no ground truth and the model can be right where the rules are not. Measured on the 10 clean texts with an earlier prompt version and pipeline.

metrics.name: Decision agreement: gpt-oss and GLM
metrics.method: same action from both models' intents, on requests where both gave a usable intent
metrics.caveat: Small sample, and only requests both models could read. Two models agreeing can both be wrong.

metrics.name: Citation validity
metrics.method: every cited (table, id) exists in the data pack
metrics.caveat: A valid citation is a real row. It does not show the row supports the claim it is cited for; context precision looks at that.

metrics.name: Referential integrity
metrics.method: id columns that point to another table (owners, workspaces, models, KPIs, assets, products, markets, lineage ends) resolve to a row
metrics.basis: data pack in data/estate.db; broken: none
metrics.caveat: Checks that references resolve, not that they are right: an asset can point to an existing but wrong owner.

metrics.name: Null or empty cells
metrics.method: share of all cells that are null or empty
metrics.basis: all 22 tables; highest columns: Data_Dictionary.unit 77%, Product_Market_Monthly.forecast_variance_pct 11%, Analytics_Assets.owner_id 6%
metrics.caveat: Some columns are empty by design (for example optional notes), so a null is not always a defect.

metrics.name: Assets with no active owner
metrics.method: no owner id, an owner id not in the Owners table, or an inactive owner
metrics.basis: 21 with no owner id at all, 0 with an unknown owner id, the rest with an inactive owner
metrics.caveat: Synthetic data, deliberately messy. Counts gaps, not how much they matter.

metrics.name: Assets sharing a name
metrics.method: assets whose name equals another asset's name
metrics.caveat: Names are not used for matching because they do not reflect coverage. Same name does not mean same content.

metrics.name: Non-canonical KPI definitions
metrics.method: KPI catalog rows whose definition status is not canonical (duplicates, conflicts, local variants)
metrics.caveat: A variant can be legitimate locally; this counts what needs a steward's decision.

metrics.name: Action accuracy (human-labelled)
metrics.method: system action equals the labeller's expected action
metrics.basis: not labelled yet: copy data/gold_labels_template.csv to data/gold_labels.csv and fill it in (docs/gold_labels.md)
metrics.caveat: Labelled by people on 20 requests at most, so one row moves a score by 5 points or more. A labeller who saw the cited rows first may lean towards the system.

metrics.name: Target accuracy (human-labelled)
metrics.method: system target equals the expected target, or both are none
metrics.basis: not labelled yet: copy data/gold_labels_template.csv to data/gold_labels.csv and fill it in (docs/gold_labels.md)
metrics.caveat: Labelled by people on 20 requests at most, so one row moves a score by 5 points or more. Several assets can be acceptable targets; this counts one.

metrics.name: KPI precision (human-labelled)
metrics.method: KPIs read that the labeller expected
metrics.basis: not labelled yet: copy data/gold_labels_template.csv to data/gold_labels.csv and fill it in (docs/gold_labels.md)
metrics.caveat: Labelled by people on 20 requests at most, so one row moves a score by 5 points or more. Only canonical KPI names are accepted.

metrics.name: KPI recall (human-labelled)
metrics.method: expected KPIs that were read
metrics.basis: not labelled yet: copy data/gold_labels_template.csv to data/gold_labels.csv and fill it in (docs/gold_labels.md)
metrics.caveat: Labelled by people on 20 requests at most, so one row moves a score by 5 points or more.

metrics.name: Cited row relevance (human-labelled)
metrics.method: cited rows the labeller marked relevant
metrics.basis: not labelled yet: copy data/gold_labels_template.csv to data/gold_labels.csv and fill it in (docs/gold_labels.md)
metrics.caveat: Labelled by people on 20 requests at most, so one row moves a score by 5 points or more. Relevance is a judgement; two labellers may differ.
